title: Chicken Piccata Pasta
description: By Anna Theoktisto: This recipe transforms classic chicken piccata into a pasta we can’t stop eating, with juicy chicken thighs cooked in a lemony, buttery sauce that clings to the pasta. The best part of chicken piccata is the lemon, butter, and caper sauce, so we added some pasta to the mix to soak it all up. Radiatori pasta — a short, ruffled pasta shape said to have been created in the 1960s and named for its resemblance to radiators — features wavy ridges which increase the surface area and hold more of the lemony, buttery piccata sauce in each bite. Serve this pasta with a green salad with lemon vinaigrette and crusty bread for mopping up any buttery sauce and leftover capers.
ingredients: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 cup cold unsalted butter (2 ounces), cubed
1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, plus lemon wedges for serving
directions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta, and cook according to package directions for al dente, about 8 minutes. (For firmer texture, reduce cooking time to 7 minutes.) Reserve 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Drain pasta; set aside.
Sprinkle chicken with salt and black pepper (maybe a little flour).

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it just begins to smoke. Add chicken, and cook, undisturbed, until browned on 1 side, about 3 minutes. Stir and cook until evenly browned, about 3 minutes.
Add garlic and crushed red pepper to skillet, and cook until fragrant and starting to brown, about 1 minute.
Add wine and capers. Bring to a boil, and reduce by half, about 1 minute.
Add reserved pasta, 1/4 cup reserved pasta cooking liquid, butter, and lemon juice.
Cook over medium, stirring occasionally, until sauce clings to pasta, about 3 minutes. (Add additional cooking liquid as needed.)
Remove from heat, and stir in Parmesan and parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
